plan.title: Entropy: Why Hot Coffee Always Cools Down
plan.description: Entropy measures how spread out energy is in a system. The second law of thermodynamics explains why isolated systems drift toward equilibrium and why some processes can't be undone.

beats.narration: Ever wonder why your coffee never heats itself back up? That's entropy. It measures how spread out energy is.
Low entropy means energy is bunched up in one spot. High entropy means it's evenly dispersed. Nature slides toward spread out.
That's the second law of thermodynamics. In an isolated system, entropy can't decrease. So some things, like cooling coffee, are irreversible.

props.text: Entropy never decreases in an isolated system.
